bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue description / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / staged default_crash_trace.txt / staged poc bytes / local OpenSC history
bug_description.normalized: The staged 768-byte witness is a little-endian length-prefixed APDU-response stream consumed by `fuzz_pkcs15_reader` via `fuzz_get_chunk()`. In the exact staged checkout, static decoding of the saved `poc` shows the first successful `LIST_OBJECTS` record starts `20 20 20 20 20 20 01 20 ... 90 20`, so `coolkey_initialize()` stores an earlier `objects_list` node with `id 0x20202020`, truncated `length 0x0120 = 288`, and `data == NULL`. The next successful `LIST_OBJECTS` record starts `20 20 20 ff 20 20 00 11 ... 90 20`, so a later node is stored with `id 0x202020ff`, truncated `length 17`, and `data == NULL`. The saved ASan allocation stack shows the crashing 17-byte region is not created while `SC_CARDCTL_COOLKEY_GET_NEXT_OBJECT` is working on stack copies; it is created later in `coolkey_find_matching_cert()` / `coolkey_find_object_by_template()` while `sc_pkcs15emu_coolkey_init()` is processing a public-key object (`pkcs15-coolkey.c:618`). In this staged tree the load-bearing bug is the comparator semantics: `coolkey_compare_id()` returns `1` on equality, but SimCList `list_locate()` treats comparator result `0` as a match, so `coolkey_find_object_by_id(..., 0x202020ff)` resolves the first non-equal list entry, namely the earlier `0x20202020` node. `coolkey_fill_object()` therefore mallocs 17 bytes for the actual first `0x202020ff` list node and then stores the same pointer into both that node and the earlier `0x20202020` node at lines 1420-1421. During `sc_disconnect_card()`, `coolkey_free_private_data()` iterates `objects_list` and frees the shared pointer once from one node and again from the other, producing the saved ASan double-free at line 819. The witness also contains a later duplicated `0x202020ff` record, but that duplicate is not the alias target that explains this staged crash. The staged `patch.diff` / reported metadata fix commit are unrelated to this path.

source.code:
unsigned long object_id = bebytes2ulong(object_info.object_id);
unsigned short object_len = bebytes2ulong(object_info.object_length);
source.description: First project-side materialization of the earlier list element that later becomes the wrong alias target.
source.value_from: Static decoding of the saved 768-byte `poc` under `fuzz_get_chunk()` semantics shows the first successful `LIST_OBJECTS` response data begins `20 20 20 20 20 20 01 20 ... 90 20`. At these statements the first four bytes become `object_id = 0x20202020`, and the next four bytes `20 20 01 20` are truncated through `unsigned short object_len` to `0x0120 = 288`.
source.note: This earlier non-duplicate entry is load-bearing because the broken comparator later returns it when the code asks for object ID `0x202020ff`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. SimCList expects comparator result `0` for a match, but this comparator returns `1` on equal IDs. `coolkey_find_object_by_id()` therefore resolves the first non-equal list element instead of the requested object.
root_cause.note: Local commit `aa6d3e1d36969aa0f955b11faf9142666145a72b` flips this comparator to `!=`. Local commit `ef61a95b31b3e70238e344d9bb0fd0b20fb649c9` later adds `if (obj_entry->length != obj->length)` in `coolkey_fill_object`, which would also reject this witness's `288`-vs-`17` alias even if the comparator bug remained.

sink.description: The second of the two aliased list elements (`0x20202020` and the first `0x202020ff`) frees the shared 17-byte buffer again during teardown.
sink.note: ASan reports `attempting double-free` on a 17-byte region `[0x6030000003d0,0x6030000003e1)` at this line, with both frees coming from `coolkey_free_private_data -> coolkey_finish -> sc_disconnect_card` and the allocation from `coolkey_fill_object:1401` on the template-search path.

tainted_value_origin.description: The later `0x202020ff` object descriptor provides the 17-byte length that drives the crashing allocation.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The next successful `LIST_OBJECTS` response begins `20 20 20 ff 20 20 00 11 ... 90 20`; `bebytes2ulong` yields `0x20200011`, and assignment to `unsigned short object_len` truncates it to `17`.

parser_admitted.description: The saved chunk stream makes applet select succeed and then returns `6d00` for `GET_STATUS(P1=1)`, so OpenSC accepts the reader as a CoolKey card and later enters `sc_pkcs15emu_coolkey_init_ex`.

copy_vs_list.description: `SC_CARDCTL_COOLKEY_GET_NEXT_OBJECT` returns a stack copy of the list entry. The crash-causing shared ownership is therefore not created by these copy-path fills; ASan shows it is created later when template search passes an actual list node into `coolkey_fill_object`.

template_search.description: ASan's allocation stack pins the crashing 17-byte allocation to this actual-list traversal while `coolkey_find_matching_cert()` is searching for a certificate for the current public-key object.

coarse_trace.summary: Object enumeration consumes attacker-controlled `LIST_OBJECTS` responses and inserts an earlier `objects_list[0] = { id 0x20202020, length 288, data NULL }` followed by `objects_list[1] = { id 0x202020ff, length 17, data NULL }`; later records exist in the witness but are not the alias target that explains the crash.
The staged comparator is inverted for SimCList: `coolkey_find_object_by_id(0x202020ff)` resolves the first non-equal list node (`objects_list[0]`) instead of the requested `0x202020ff` node.

Certificate matching switches from `GET_NEXT_OBJECT` stack copies to an actual-list scan; when that scan reaches the first 17-byte `0x202020ff` node, `coolkey_fill_object` allocates 17 bytes and stores the same pointer into `objects_list[1]` and the misresolved earlier `objects_list[0]` node.
Card teardown iterates `objects_list`; one of the aliased nodes frees the shared 17-byte buffer first and the other frees the same pointer again, matching the AddressSanitizer double-free.

fine_trace.code:
unsigned long object_id = bebytes2ulong(object_info.object_id);
unsigned short object_len = bebytes2ulong(object_info.object_length);
fine_trace.note: Source. The first successful `LIST_OBJECTS` response in the saved chunk stream begins `20 20 20 20 20 20 01 20 ...`. These lines materialize the earlier list element as `object_id = 0x20202020`; because `object_len` is an `unsigned short`, the big-endian length `0x20200120` is truncated here to `288`.

This append creates `objects_list[0]` with `id == 0x20202020`, `length == 288`, and `data == NULL`. Its head-of-list position is load-bearing because the broken comparator later stops on this non-equal node when asked for `0x202020ff`.

fine_trace.code:
unsigned long object_id = bebytes2ulong(object_info.object_id);
unsigned short object_len = bebytes2ulong(object_info.object_length);
fine_trace.note: The next successful `LIST_OBJECTS` response begins `20 20 20 ff 20 20 00 11 ...`, so the loop materializes a later list element with `object_id = 0x202020ff` and truncated `object_len = 17`.

This append creates `objects_list[1]` with `id == 0x202020ff`, `length == 17`, and `data == NULL`, immediately after `objects_list[0]`. The saved witness later adds more list records, including another `0x202020ff`, but the crashing alias below uses these first two elements.

Root cause. SimCList `list_locate()` stops when the comparator returns `0` (`src/common/simclist.c:686`), but this comparator returns `1` when IDs are equal and `0` when they differ. For the list order from steps 2 and 4, `coolkey_find_object_by_id(..., 0x202020ff)` therefore resolves `objects_list[0]`, the earlier non-equal `0x20202020` entry.

Unlike `SC_CARDCTL_COOLKEY_GET_NEXT_OBJECT` (`card-coolkey.c:1289-1290`), this path passes a live list element into `coolkey_find_attribute`. The saved ASan allocation stack reaches the crash through this actual-list traversal while `sc_pkcs15emu_coolkey_init()` is in its public-key case (`pkcs15-coolkey.c:618`), and the first 17-byte `0x202020ff` node encountered in this head-to-tail scan is `objects_list[1]` from step 4.
For this actual `objects_list[1]` node, `obj->length == 17` and `obj->data == NULL`, so line 1401 allocates the 17-byte region later reported by ASan.

With the staged comparator semantics from step 5, `coolkey_find_object_by_id(..., 0x202020ff)` resolves `objects_list[0]`, not `objects_list[1]`. Because this call is filling an actual list node from step 6, lines 1420-1421 store the same `new_obj_data` pointer into both `objects_list[0].data` and `objects_list[1].data`. Here the aliased nodes have different stored lengths (`288` versus `17`); local commit `ef61a95b` later adds an explicit guard for that mismatch.
During `sc_disconnect_card()` teardown, list iteration reaches one of the two aliased list elements from step 8 (`objects_list[0]` or `objects_list[1]`) and frees the shared 17-byte buffer once.

Sink. A later cleanup iteration reaches the other aliased list element and calls `free` on the same pointer again. AddressSanitizer reports this second free here, with the allocation from step 7 and the first free from step 9.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` / metadata `reported_fixed_commit` `2d02de4233a70fdad4cbf0862c83f03d9ba85d78` address unrelated `coolkey_get_cplc_data` handling for OSS-Fuzz issue 18990, not this comparator-driven alias. In the exact staged history, `aa6d3e1d36969aa0f955b11faf9142666145a72b` is the earliest direct fix because it makes `coolkey_find_object_by_id()` match equal IDs; `ef61a95b31b3e70238e344d9bb0fd0b20fb649c9` later adds the missing `obj_entry->length != obj->length` check that independently blocks this witness's `288`-vs-`17` alias; `c246f6f69a749d4f68626b40795a4f69168008f4` later rejects duplicate IDs but is not necessary to explain the observed crash.

format.name: fuzz_get_chunk card-response stream
format.contract: A little-endian length-prefixed chunk stream consumed by `fuzz_pkcs15_reader` via `fuzz_get_chunk()`. The saved witness must make `coolkey_match_card()` succeed, then feed `coolkey_initialize()` a `LIST_OBJECTS` record beginning `20 20 20 20 20 20 01 20` and a later `LIST_OBJECTS` record beginning `20 20 20 ff 20 20 00 11`, so `priv->objects_list` contains an earlier `0x20202020`/`288` node and a later `0x202020ff`/`17` node. The same run then has to reach `coolkey_find_matching_cert()` / `coolkey_find_object_by_template()`, where the staged broken comparator makes the first actual `0x202020ff` node alias its 17-byte buffer into the earlier `0x20202020` node and teardown double-frees it.
